title: Minister says Canada’s national AI literacy training will go live next month | BetaKit
html:
Canada’s national AI literacy program will roll out nationwide next month, according to federal AI Minister Evan Solomon.

The news: Solomon broke the news in an as-yet unaired episode of The BetaKit Podcast, telling BetaKit editor-in-chief Douglas Soltys that the much-anticipated literacy program would be available to all Canadians this December. Solomon did not elaborate on what the rollout would look like, or offer specific dates as to when in December to expect the launch, but did say the nationwide programming would take participants about 90 minutes to complete.

From the source: “In December, you’ll see the national literacy program roll out for every single Canadian. This one is for every Canadian—my mom; anybody—and it’s 90 minutes,” Solomon said.

The context: Launching AI literacy training for the general public would be the third and final program delivered as part of Ottawa’s larger National AI Literacy Initiative, which Solomon unveiled in September. Under that framework, the federal government launched a three-hour training course for post-secondary students, as well as an Essentials for Educators course for teachers. It has previously stated that those courses would reach as many as one million students and 50,000 educators.

The $13-million initiative was first outlined in Canada’s National AI Strategy. The government tapped the Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute (Amii) to lead development of the program’s curriculum and its delivery to Canadians.

Final thought: Programming is intended to help learners gain the skills to “more confidently and responsibly” use AI. Solomon’s ministry previously said that training will focus on developing the skills needed to assess AI-generated content, identify misinformation, bias, or privacy concerns, and to provide “practical learning opportunities.” These training initiatives have been central to Ottawa’s efforts to increase AI adoption and trust among Canadians, given that some studies indicate Canada lags behind when it comes to both categories.

BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.

summary: National rollout will scale programming to just 90 minutes and will be available to all Canadians. The post Minister says Canada’s national AI literacy training will go live next month first appeared on BetaKit .
